links.outcome: Calibration of LLM self-reported confidence: correlation with accuracy and confidence gap between correct and incorrect answers
links.effect: Correlation between mean confidence for correct answers and accuracy was inverse (r=-0.40; P=.001). Confidence difference between correct and incorrect responses ranged 0.6% to 5.4%; GPT-4o highest (5.4%, P=.003).
links.quote: The correlation between the mean confidence scores for correct answers and model accuracy was inverse and statistically significant (r=-0.40; P=.001), indicating that worse-performing models exhibited paradoxically higher confidence.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study evaluating the confidence calibration and accuracy of 12 LLMs across clinical multiple-choice questions without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
